title: Backflow installation code workflow: verify the governing rule before design
description: Use the governing program and adopted code to confirm approval responsibility, inspection, testing, and filing before backflow installation design or purchase.
prompt: What must be known before this work can be closed out?
answer: The code workflow identifies who approves the design, inspection, testing, and closeout. Use the installation decision page for device selection and field-detail planning.
urgency: Treat deadlines, active discharge, damaged bodies, critical service, or uncertain authority requirements as reasons to use a qualified path.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: Identify the exact assembly, model, size, and protected system.
Separate design approval, inspection, certified testing, report submission, and approval responsibility.
Retain the final proof with the property asset record.

choices.label: I need device and field requirements
choices.detail: Use the installation decision page for assembly, placement, drainage, access, and closeout details.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Identify the authority
steps.body: Confirm the utility, adopted code, permit authority, fire authority, and any plan-review owner.

steps.title: Define approval responsibility
steps.body: Separate design, installation, inspection, certified testing, report submission, and correction ownership.

steps.title: Retain the closeout evidence
steps.body: Keep the approved plan, permit or inspection result, final test, and official confirmation together.

safeChecks: Confirm the official issuer and eligible tester requirement before booking work.
Use the exact manufacturer record for assembly orientation and installation limitations.
Keep approved plans, failed records, and completed records where correction or retesting is required.
stopConditions: Do not assume a plumbing permit replaces utility or fire-authority approval.
Do not approve work without identifying the exact assembly, authority, and closeout scope.
notThisDevice: This code workflow does not select a universal backflow assembly.
A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
Use the installation decision page for device selection and field-detail planning.
evidenceNote: Use the adopted code, governing utility or authority instructions, and exact manufacturer record to validate the final path.
